stories.representative_title: Will Pochettino fix Manchester United? Put your questions to Will Unwin

items.title: Will Pochettino fix Manchester United? Put your questions to Will Unwin
items.summary:
As Mauricio Pochettino prepares for his first game in charge at Anfield, the Guardian’s Will Unwin will answer your questions on Manchester United’s new head coach, the crisis he inherits and what comes next.

Ask a question: log in or sign up here

Manchester United have a new head coach. Mauricio Pochettino has signed a two-and-a-half-year deal to replace Michael Carrick, who was sacked after leading the club to their worst start to a season in four decades.

In a tearful farewell to the US men’s national team, Pochettino called the move “one of the most difficult decisions” of his career. But the job he inherits may be harder still. No team in Europe’s top five leagues has conceded more goals in all competitions this season. Bruno Fernandes has rejected a second offer of a new contract. And fans have turned their anger on the hierarchy above the dugout.

stories.representative_title: Manchester United’s infamous 1974 relegation is a warning from history

items.title: Manchester United’s infamous 1974 relegation is a warning from history
items.summary:
It may have been a different era, but the 1970s contain salutary lessons for a club in serious decline once again

In many ways, there are striking parallels between the Manchester United relegated in 1974 and the Manchester United sitting in the relegation zone at this stage of the season for the first time in 40 years. A legendary manager leaves, his shadow remains; with boardroom dithering and uncertainty, his replacements churn and burn as the club slide over several years.

Sir Matt Busby stepped aside as manager of the 1968 European Cup-winning side, but stayed on as a director, just as Sir Alex Ferguson did, watching from the Old Trafford directors’ box as successors tried and failed.

stories.representative_title: ‘An honour’: Pochettino up for challenge of leading Manchester United revival

items.title: ‘An honour’: Pochettino up for challenge of leading Manchester United revival
items.summary:
• New head coach faces tough opening match at Anfield

  • ‘It’s a big challenge but at the same time it’s adrenaline’

Mauricio Pochettino said it was “an honour” and “a privilege” to be the new Manchester United head coach after arriving in England on Wednesday.

Pochettino flew from Cincinnati to Manchester overnight after overseeing the USA beating Haiti in his final game in charge. Members of Pochettino’s staff landed earlier in the week to begin work at Carrington, laying the foundations as United seek to turn their season around. His right-hand man, Jesús Pérez, the goalkeeping coach Toni Jiménez and the fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino, who continues to work with his father, have already taken training with those not on international duty.

stories.representative_title: Mauricio Pochettino’s USMNT time will be remembered fondly, but it wasn’t transformational

items.title: Mauricio Pochettino’s USMNT time will be remembered fondly, but it wasn’t transformational
items.summary:
The incoming Manchester United manager improved the US team’s culture and competitiveness, but could not bring about sea change in two years

In a theater high up in a midtown Manhattan skyscraper built from lots of glass, a highlight reel played to deafening music. And then, on “a monumental day for US Soccer”, federation president, Cindy Parlow Cone, announced they had bagged their man, Mauricio Pochettino, to become the highest-profile United States manager in the men’s national team’s history.

Pochettino held court for three-quarters of an hour in his signature blend of Spanglish before the assembled media and a grab bag of sponsors. Then he recorded some TV hits. And after that, in a bit of accidental prescience, he went off to record a podcast with Gary Neville.

items.title: Football Daily | From Cincinnati to Manchester: Pochettino in a hurry to paint town red
items.summary:
Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!

With his team mired in the relegation zone and a massive match at Liverpool this weekend, Mauricio Pochettino has been understandably busy since being appointed head coach of Manchester United. Unfortunately for Old Trafford regulars, the small print of his contract meant the Argentinian was tied up masterminding victory for USA USA USA in the second leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti when he ought to have been in Carrington moving red magnets around a tactics board in front of Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo and Harry Maguire.
